verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              वर्तमाने तदा युद्धे घोररूपे भयानके। अभज्यत बलं तत्र तव पुत्रस्य पाण्डवैः॥१॥
तांस्तु यत्नेन महता सन्निवार्य महारथान्। पुत्रस्ते योधयामास पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्॥२॥
निवृत्ताः सहसा योधास्तव पुत्रजयैषिणः। सन्निवृत्तेषु तेष्वेवं युद्धमासीत्सुदारुणम्॥३॥
verses.english: The Kuru warriors, seeking your son's welfare, suddenly came back. Upon their return, the battle once more became fearful, between your warriors and those of the foe, resembling that between the gods and the Asuras in the days of yore. Neither amongst the enemies nor amongst your people was there a single warrior who fled away from the field.

verses.sanskrit: तावकानां परेषां च देवासुररणोपमम्। परेषां तव सैन्ये वा नासीत्कश्चित्पराङ्मुखः॥४॥
अनुमानेन युध्यन्ते संज्ञाभिश्च परस्परम्। तेषां क्षयो महानासीद्युध्यतामितरेतरम्॥५॥
verses.english: The warriors fought, knowing one another by the names they uttered. A great onslaught took place there.

verses.sanskrit: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा क्रोधेन महता युतः। जिगीषमाणः सङ्ग्रामे धार्तराष्ट्रान्सराजकान्॥६॥
त्रिभिः शारद्वतं विद्ध्वा रुक्मपुङ्खः शिलाशितैः। चतुर्भिर्निजघानाश्वान्नाराचैः कृतवर्मणः॥७॥
verses.english: Filled with great anger and desirous of defeating the Dhartarashtras and their king in that battle, king Yudhishthira struck the son of Sharadvata with three gold winged arrows whetted on stone and next killed with four others the four horses of Kritavarman.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वत्थामा तु हार्दिक्यमपोवाह यशस्विनम्। अथ शारद्वतोऽष्टाभिः प्रत्यविद्ध्यद्युधिष्ठिरम्॥८॥
verses.english: Then Ashvatthaman carried away the celebrated son of Hridika. Sharadvat's son struck Yudhishthira in return with eight arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा रथान्सप्तशतान् रणे। प्रैषयद्यत्र राजासौ धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥९॥
verses.english: Then king Duryodhana sent seven hundred cars to the place where king Yudhishthira was fighting.

verses.sanskrit: ते रथा रथिभिर्युक्ता मनोमारुतरंहसः। अभ्यद्रवन्त सङ्ग्रामे कौन्तेयस्य रथं प्रति॥१०॥
ते समन्तान्महाराज परिवार्य युधिष्ठिरम्। अदृश्यं सायकैश्चक्रुर्मेघा इव दिवाकरम्॥११॥
ते दृष्ट्वा धर्मराजानं कौरवेयैस्तथा कृतम्। नामृष्यन्त सुसंरब्धाः शिखण्डिप्रमुखा रथाः॥१२॥
verses.english: Then Pandava heroes, led by Shikhandin, beholding king Yudhishthira assailed in that way by the Kauravas, were filled with rage and unable to put up with it.

verses.sanskrit: रथैरश्ववरैर्युक्तैः किङ्किणीजालसंवृतैः। आजग्मुरथ रक्षन्तः कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्॥१३॥
ततः प्रववृते रौद्रः सङ्ग्रामः शोणितोदकः। पाण्डवानां कुरूणां च यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनः॥१४॥
रथान्सप्तशतान्हत्वा कुरूणामाततायिनाम्। पाण्डवाः सह पञ्चालैः पुनरेवाभ्यवारयन्॥१५॥
verses.english: Killing those seven hundred hostile carwarriors of the Kuru army, the Pandavas and the Panchalas once more resisted (the whole Kuru ariny).

verses.sanskrit: तत्र युद्धं महच्चासीत्तव पुत्रस्य पाण्डवैः। न च तत्तादृशं दृष्टं नैव चापि परिश्रुतम्॥१६॥
वर्तमाने तदा युद्धे निर्मर्यादे समन्ततः। वध्यमानेषु योधेषु तावकेष्वितरेषु च॥१७॥
विनदत्सु च योधेषु शङ्खवर्यैश्च पूरितैः। उत्क्रुष्टैः सिंहनादैश्च गर्जितैश्चैव धन्विनाम्॥१८॥
verses.english: During the onset of that battle in which no consideration was shown by any party for another and while the warriors of your army and those of the foe were being killed quickly, the coinbatants were all shouting and blowing their conchs. The bowmen were roaring and uttering loud noises of diverse kinds.

verses.sanskrit: अतिप्रवृत्ते युद्धे च छिद्यमानेषु मर्मसु। धावमानेषु योधेषु जयगृद्धिषु मारिष॥१९॥
verses.english: The very vitals of the combatants were being struck, during that fight and the troops, O sire, desirous of victory, were rushing with speed.

verses.sanskrit: संहारे सर्वतो जाते पृथिव्यां शोकसम्भवे। बह्वीनामुत्तमस्त्रीणां सीमन्तोद्धरणे तथा॥२०॥
verses.english: Everything on carth was under-going ai woeful destruction, during that battle when numberless ladies of birth and beauty were being made widows.

verses.sanskrit: निर्मर्यादे महायुद्धे वर्तमाने सुदारुणे। प्रादुरासन्विनाशाय तदोत्पाताः सुदारुणाः॥२१॥
verses.english: During the progress of that fierce encounter in which the warriors fought without any consideration for friends and foes, evil omens appeared, presaging the destruction of everything.

verses.sanskrit: चचाल शब्दं कुर्वाणा सपर्वतवना मही। सदण्डाः सोल्मुका राजन् कीर्यमाणाः समन्ततः॥२२॥
उल्काः पेतुर्दिवो भूमावाहत्य रविमण्डलम्। विष्वग्वाताः प्रादुरासन्नीचैः शर्करवर्षिणः॥२३॥
अश्रूणि मुमुचुर्नागा वेपथुं चास्पृशन्भृशम्। एतान् घोराननादृत्य समुत्पातान्सुदारुणान्॥२४॥
पुनर्युद्धाय संयत्ताः क्षत्रियास्तस्थुरव्यथाः। रमणीये कुरुक्षेत्रे पुण्ये स्वर्गं यियासवः॥२५॥
ततो गान्धारराजस्य पुत्रः शकुनिरब्रवीत्। युद्ध्यध्वमग्रतो यावत्पृष्ठतो हन्मि पाण्डवान्॥२६॥
verses.english: Then Shakuni, the son of the Gandhara king, said-"Fight you all in front! I, however, will kill the Pandavas from behind!”_-Then the active Madraka warriors, amongst those on our side that were advancing, were filled with joy and uttered various cries. Others also did the same.

verses.sanskrit: ततो नः सम्प्रयातानां मद्रयोधास्तरस्विनः। हृष्टाः किलकिलाशब्दमकुर्वन्त परे तथा॥२७॥
अस्मांस्तु पुनरासाद्य लब्धलक्षा दुरासदाः। शरासनानि धुन्वन्तः शरवर्षैरवाकिरन्॥२८॥
verses.english: The invincible and sure-armed Pandavas, once more coming against us, shook their bows and enshrouded us with showers of arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततो हतं परैस्तत्र मद्रराजबलं तदा। दुर्योधनबलं दृष्ट्वा पुनरासीत् पराङ्मुखम्॥२९॥
verses.english: The army of the Madrakas then were killed by the foc. Beholding this, the troops of Duryodhana once more fled from the battle.

verses.sanskrit: गान्धारराजस्तु पुनर्वाक्यमाह ततो बली। निवर्तध्वमधर्मज्ञा युध्यध्वं किं सृतेन वः॥३०॥
verses.english: The might king of the Gandharas, however, once more said these words-"Stop, you sinful wretches, fight with the foe. What use is there of fight.” At that time, O foremost of Bharata's race, the king of the Gandharas had full ten thousand horsemen capable of fighting with bright lances.

verses.sanskrit: अनीकं दशसाहस्रमश्वानां भरतर्षभ। आसीद्गान्धारराजस्य विशालप्रासयोधिनाम्॥३१॥
बलेन तेन विक्रम्य वर्तमाने जनक्षये। पृष्ठतः पाण्डवानीकमभ्यघ्नन्निशितैः शरैः॥३२॥
verses.english: During the onset of that great carnage, Shakuni, aided by the force, displayed his valor and assailed the Pandava army at the rear, killing it with his keen arrows.

verses.sanskrit: तदभ्रमिव वातेन क्षिप्यमाणं समन्ततः। अभज्यत महाराज पाण्डूनां सुमहद्बलम्॥३३॥
verses.english: The huge force of the Pandus then, O king, were dispersed even as a mass of clouds of all sides by a powerful wind.

verses.sanskrit: ततो युधिष्ठिरः प्रेक्ष्य भग्नं स्वबलमन्तिकात्। अभ्यनादयदव्यग्रः सहदेवं महाबलम्॥३४॥
verses.english: Then beholding his own army rouled, Yudhishthira coolly urged the mighty Sahadeva, saying-"Yonder the son of Subala, afflicting our rear, stands clad in mail. He kills our forces. Behold that wicked man, O son of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: असौ सुबलपुत्रो नो जघनं पीड्य दंशितः। सैन्यानि सूदयत्येष पश्य पाण्डव दुर्मतिम्॥३५॥
गच्छ त्वं द्रौपदेयैश्च शकुनिं सौबलं जहि। रथनीकमहं धक्ष्ये पञ्चालसहितोऽनघ॥३६॥
verses.english: Helped by the sons of Draupadi proceed towards him and kill Shakuni, the son of Subala. Supported by the Panchalas, O sinless one, I will meanwhile kill the car-force of the enemy.

verses.sanskrit: गच्छन्तु कुञ्जराः सर्वे वाजिनश्च सह त्वया। पादाताश्च त्रिसाहस्राः शकुनिं तैर्वृतो जहि॥३७॥
ततो गजाः सप्तशताश्चापपाणिभिरास्थिताः। पञ्च चाश्वसहस्राणि सहदेवश्च वीर्यवान्॥३८॥
verses.english: Let all the elephants and all the horse and three thousand foot go with you. Helped by these, slay Shakuni.” At this seven hundred elephants ridden by bowmen and five thousand horse and the valiant Sahadeva and three thousand foot-soldiers and the son of Draupadi, all proceeded against invincible Shakuni.

verses.sanskrit: पादाताश्च त्रिसाहस्रा द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः। रणे ह्यभ्येद्रवंस्ते तु शकुनिं युद्धदुर्मदम्॥३९॥
ततस्तु सौबलो राजन्नभ्यतिक्रम्य पाण्डवान्। जघान पृष्ठतः सेनां जयगृद्धः प्रतापवान्॥४०॥
verses.english: However, O king, overpowering the Pandavas and longing for victory, Subala's son, of great valour, began to slay their forces from the back.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वरोहास्तु संरब्धाः पाण्डवानां तरस्विनाम्। प्राविशन्सौबलानीकमभ्यतिक्रम्य तान् रथान्॥४१॥
verses.english: The horsemen, beside themselves with rage, of the Pandavas penetrated the division of Subala's son, overpowering the latter's carwarriors.

verses.sanskrit: ते तत्र सादिनाः शूराः सौबलस्य महद्बलम्। रणमध्ये व्यतिष्ठन्त शरवर्षैरवाकिरन्॥४२॥
verses.english: Those heroic horsemen, staying in the midst of their own elephants, enshrouded the large host of Subala's son with showers of arrows.

verses.sanskrit: तदुद्यतगदाप्रासमाकपुरुषसेवितम्। प्रावर्तत महद्युद्धं राजन्दुर्मन्त्रिते तव॥४३॥
verses.english: On account of your evil counsels, O king, a dreadful battle took place in which maces and lances were used and in which heroes only took part.

verses.sanskrit: उपारमन्त ज्याशब्दाः प्रेक्षका रथिनोऽभवन्। न हि स्वेषां परेषां वा विशेषः प्रत्यदृश्यत॥४४॥
verses.english: The twang of bows was no longer heard there, for all the car-warriors stood there as spectators. At that time no difference could be seen between the opposing parties.

verses.sanskrit: शूरबाहुविसृष्टानां शक्तीनां भरतर्षभ। ज्योतिषामिव सम्पातमपश्यन्कुरुपाण्डवाः॥४५॥
verses.english: Both the Kurus and the Pandavas, O foremost of Bharatas, saw the darts, shot off heroic arms, pass like meteors through the sky.

verses.sanskrit: ऋष्टिभिर्विमलाभिश्च तत्र तत्र विशाम्पते। सम्पतन्तीभिराकाशमावृतं बह्वशोभत॥४६॥
verses.english: The entire sky, O king, covered with falling and bright sword, appeared highly beautiful.

verses.sanskrit: प्रासानां पततां राजन् रूपमासीत्समन्ततः। शलभानामिवाकाशे तदा भरतसत्तम॥४७॥
verses.english: The view presented, O best of the Bharatas, by the lances hurled all around, was like that of swarms of locusts in the sky.

verses.sanskrit: रुधिरोक्षितसर्वाङ्गा विप्रविद्धैर्नियन्तृभिः। हयाः परिपतन्ति स्म शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥४८॥
verses.english: Horses, with limbs covered with blood on account of wounds inflicted by horsemen themselves struck with arrows, dropped down on all sides in hundreds and thousands.

verses.sanskrit: अन्योयं परिपिष्टाश्च समासाद्य परस्परम्। आविक्षताः स्म दृश्यन्ते वमन्तो रुधिरं मुखैः॥४९॥
verses.english: They all remained huddled together. many of them were wounded and many vomited blood. A thick darkness set in there when the troops were covered with a cloud of dust.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽभवत्तमो घोरं सैन्येन रजसा वृते। तानपाक्रमतोऽद्राक्षं तस्माद्देशादरिन्दम॥५०॥
verses.english: When that darkness covered everything, O king, we saw those brave heroes, horses and men move away from that spot.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वान् राजन्मनुष्यांश्च रजसा संवृते सति। भूमौ निपतिताश्चान्ये वमन्तो रुधिरं बहु॥५१॥
verses.english: Others dropped down on the earth vomiting blood profusely. Many warriors, entangled with one another by their locks, could not move.

verses.sanskrit: केशाकेशि समालग्ना न शेकुश्चेष्टितुं नराः। अन्योन्यमश्वपृष्ठेभ्यो विकर्षन्तो महाबलाः॥५२॥
verses.english: Many powerful heroes dragged one another from the backs of their horses and encountering one another thus, killed one another like wrestlers. Many, deprived of life, were carried away by the horses they rode.

verses.sanskrit: मल्ला इव समासाद्य निजघ्नुरितरेतरम्। अश्वैश्च व्यपकृष्यन्त बहवोऽत्र गतासवः॥५३॥
भूमौ निपतिताश्चान्ये बहवो विजयैषिणः। तत्र तत्र व्यदृश्यन्त पुरुषाः शूरमानिनः॥५४॥
रक्तोक्षितैश्छिन्नभुजैरवकृष्टशिरोरुहैः। व्यदृश्यत मही कीर्णा शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥५५॥
दूरं न शक्यं तत्रासीद्गन्तुमश्वेन केनचित्। साश्वारोहैर्हतैरश्वैरावृते वसुधातले॥५६॥
रुधिरोक्षितसन्नाहैरात्तशस्त्रैरुदायुधैः। नानाप्रहरणैर्घोरैः परस्परवधैषिभिः॥५७॥
verses.english: The surface of the earth being covered with clephant-riders and horsemen and killed horses and warriors with blood-stained armours and those armed with weapons and those who had tried to kill one another with various kinds of terrible weapons, all lying in a mass in that lifedestroying battle, no warrior could proceed far on his horse.

verses.sanskrit: सुसन्निकृष्टैः सङ्ग्रामे हतभूयिष्ठसैनिकैः। स मुहूर्तं ततो युद्ध्वा सौबलोऽथ विशाम्पते॥५८॥
षट्साहस्रैर्हयैः शिष्टैरपायाच्छकुनिस्ततः। तथैव पाण्डवानीकं रुधिरेण समुक्षितम्॥५९॥
verses.english: Having fought for a little while, Shakuni, the son of Subala, O king, went away from that spot with the remnant of his cavalry, six thousand in number. Similarly the Pandava force, covered with blood and its animals worn out, moved away from there with its remnant consisting of six thousand horse.

verses.sanskrit: षट्साहस्रैर्हयैः शिष्टैरपायाच्छान्तवाहनम्। अश्वारोहाश्च पाण्डूनामब्रुवन् रुधिरोक्षिताः॥६०॥
सुसन्निकृष्टे सङ्ग्रामे भूयिष्ठे त्यक्तजीविताः। न हि शक्यं स्थैर्योद्धुं कुत एव महागजैः॥६१॥
verses.english: Horsemen, covered with blood of the Pandava army then, determined upon fighting and prepared to sacrifice their lives, said-"It is no longer possible to fight here on cars; how much more difficult it is then to fight here on elephants against elephants.

verses.sanskrit: रथानेव रथा यान्तु कुञ्जराः कुञ्जरानपि। प्रतियातो हि शकुनिः स्वमनीकमवस्थितः॥६२॥
न पुनः सौबलो राजा युद्धमभ्यागमिष्यति। ततस्तु द्रौपदेयाश्च ते च मत्ता महाद्विपाः॥६३॥
verses.english: Having retreated Shakuni is now staying within his own detachment. The royal son of Subala will not again come to fight.”

verses.sanskrit: प्रययुर्यत्र पाञ्चाल्यो धृष्टद्युम्नो महारथः। सहदेवोऽपि कौरव्य रजोमेघे समुत्थिते॥६४॥
verses.english: Then the sons of Draupadi and those infuriate elephants went where the Panchala prince Dhrishtadyumna, that great car-warrior, was.

verses.sanskrit: एकाकी प्रययौ तत्र यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः। ततस्तेषु प्रयातेषु शकुनिः सौबलः पुनः॥६५॥
verses.english: Sahadeva also, when that cloud of dust set in, went alone where king Yudhishthira was.

verses.sanskrit: पार्श्वतोऽभ्यहनत्क्रुद्धो धृष्टद्युम्नस्य वाहिनीम्। तत्पुनस्तुमुलं युद्धं प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वाभ्यवर्तत॥६६॥
verses.english: After all those had departed Shakuni the son of Subala, worked up with wrath, once more attacked. Dhrishtadyumna's division and began to strike it.

verses.sanskrit: तावकानां परेषां च परस्परवधैषिणाम्। ते चान्योन्यमवैक्षन्त तस्मिन् वीरसमागमे॥६७॥
verses.english: Again a dreadful encounter took place, in which the combatants did not care for their lives, between your soldiers and those of the foe, all of whom were desirous of killing one another.

verses.sanskrit: योधाः पर्यपतन् राजन् शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। असिभिश्छिद्यमानानां शिरसां लोकसंक्षये॥६८॥
verses.english: In that encounter of heroes, the combatants first looked at one another steadfastly and then rushed, O king and attacked one another in hundreds and thousands.

verses.sanskrit: प्रादुरासीन्महाशब्दस्तालानां पततामिव। विमुक्तानां शरीराणां छिन्नानां पततां भुवि॥६९॥
verses.english: In that onslaught, heads, cut off with swords, dropped down with a noise like that of falling palmyra fruits.

verses.sanskrit: सायुधानां च बाहूनामुरूणां च विशाम्पते। आसीत्कटकटाशब्दः सुमहाँल्लोमहर्षणः॥७०॥
verses.english: Loud noise also arose making the very hairs stand erect, of bodies falling down on the ground, divested of armours and wounded with weapons and of falling weapons also, O king and of arms and thighs cut off from the trunk.

verses.sanskrit: निघ्नन्तो निशितैः शस्त्रैर्भातॄन्पुत्रान्सखीनपि। योधाः परिपतन्ति स्म यथामिषकृते खगाः॥७१॥
verses.english: Assailing brothers and sons and even fathers with keen weapons, the combatants fought like birds, for a piece of meat.

verses.sanskrit: अन्योन्यं प्रतिसंरब्धाः समासाद्य परस्परम्। अहं पूर्वमहं पूर्वमिति निघ्नन्सहस्रशः॥७२॥
सङ्घातेनासनभ्रष्टैरश्वारोहैर्गतासुभिः। हयाः परिपतन्ति स्म शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥७३॥
स्फुरतां प्रतिविष्टानामश्वानां शीघ्रगामिनाम्। स्तनतां च मनुष्याणां सन्नद्धानां विशाम्पते॥७४॥
verses.english: There arose loud noise of neighing horses of great flectness and of shouting men clad in mail and of the falling darts and swords, O king, of combatants desirous of cutting one another to the very quick on account, O monarch, of your evil policy.

verses.sanskrit: शक्त्यृष्टिप्रासशब्दश्च तुमुलः समपद्यत। भिन्दतां परमर्माणि राजन् दुर्मन्त्रिते तव॥७५॥
श्रमाभिभूताः सरंब्धाः श्रान्तवाहाः पिपासवः। विक्षताश्च शितैः शस्त्रैरभ्यवर्तन्त तावकाः॥७६॥
verses.english: At that time, your soldiers, exhausted and worked up with rage, their animals fatigued, themselves thirsty, wounded with sharp weapons, began to turn away from the battle.

verses.sanskrit: मत्ता रुधिरगन्धेन बहवोऽत्र विचेतसः। जघ्नुः परान्स्वकांश्चैव प्राप्तान्प्राप्ताननन्तरान्॥७७॥
बहवश्च गतप्राणाः क्षत्रिया जयगृद्धिनः। भूमावभ्यपतन् राजन् शरवृष्टिभिरावृताः॥७८॥
verses.english: O king, actuated with the desire of victory, large numbers of Kshatriyas were struck down with arrows and lay prostrate on the earth.

verses.sanskrit: वृकगृध्रशृगालानां तुमुले मोदनेऽहनि। आसीद्बलक्षयो घोरस्तव पुत्रस्य पश्यतः॥७९॥
verses.english: Wolves, vultures and jackals began to yell hideously in joy. In the very presence of your son your son army suffered a great loss.

verses.sanskrit: नराश्वकायैः सञ्छन्ना भूमिरासीद्विशाम्पते। रुधिरोदकचित्रा च भीरूणां भयवर्धिनी॥८०॥
असिभिः पट्टिशैः शूलैस्तक्षमाणाः पुनः पुनः। तावकाः पाण्डवेयाश्च न न्यवर्तन्त भारत॥८१॥
verses.english: Struck and wounded repeatedly with swords and battle-axes and lances, your warriors, as also the Pandavas, O Bharata, ceased to approach one another.

verses.sanskrit: प्रहरन्तो यथाशक्ति यावत्प्राणस्य धारणम्। योधाः परिपतन्ति स्म वमन्तो रुधिरं व्रणैः॥८२॥
verses.english: Striking one another according to their might and fighting to the last combatants dropped down, bleeding.

verses.sanskrit: शिरो गृहीत्वा केशेषु कबन्धः स्म प्रदृश्यते। उद्यम्य च शितं खड्गं रुधिरेण परिप्लुतम्॥८३॥
verses.english: Headless from were seen, catching the hair of their heads and holding swords stained in blood.

verses.sanskrit: तथोत्थितेषु बहुषु कबधेषु नराधिप। तथा रुधिरगन्धेन योधाः कश्मलमाविशन्॥८४॥
verses.english: When many headless forms, O king, had thus rise up, when the smell of blood had made the warriors almost senseless and the loud noise had somewhat subsided, Subala's son again approached the large army of the Pandavas, with the small remnant of his cavalry.

verses.sanskrit: मन्दीभूते ततः शब्दे पाण्डवानां महद्बलम्। अल्पावशिष्टैस्तुरगैरभ्यवर्तत सौबलः॥८५॥
ततोऽभ्यधावंस्त्वरिताः पाण्डवा जयगृद्धिनः। पदातयश्च नागाश्च सादिनश्चोद्यतायुधाः॥८६॥
कोष्ठकीकृत्य चाप्येनं परिक्षिप्य च सर्वशः। शस्त्रैर्नानाविधैर्जघ्नुर्युद्धपारं तितीर्षवः॥८७॥
verses.english: Desirous of terminating the hostilities, the Pandavas, forming a wall, encircled Shakuni on all sides and began to strike him with various kinds of weapons.

verses.sanskrit: त्वदीयास्तांस्तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य सर्वतः समभिद्रुतान्। रथाश्वपत्तिद्विरदाः पाण्डवनभिदुद्रुवुः॥८८॥
verses.english: Beholding your soldiers assailed from every side, the Kauravas, with horse, foot, elephants and cars, rushed towards the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: केचित्पदातयः पद्भिर्मुष्टिभिश्च परस्परम्। निजघ्नुः समरे शूराः क्षीणशस्त्रास्ततोऽपतन्॥८९॥
verses.english: Some brave foot-soldiers, destitute of weapons, attacked their foes in that battle, with feet and fists and struck them down.

verses.sanskrit: रथेभ्यो रथिनः पेतुर्द्विपेभ्यो हस्तिसादिनः। विमानेभ्यो दिवो भ्रष्टाः सिद्धाः पुण्यक्षयादिव॥९०॥
verses.english: Car-warriors dropped down from cars and elephant-men from elephants, like virtuous persons falling down from their celestial vehicles upon the wane of their virtue.

verses.sanskrit: एवमन्योन्यमायत्ता योधा जघ्नुर्महाहवे। पितॄन् भ्रातॄन्वयस्यांश्च पुत्रानापि तथा परे॥९१॥
verses.english: Thus the warriors fought with one another in that great battle and killed fathers and brothers and friends and sons.

verses.sanskrit: एवमासीदमर्यादं युद्धं भरतसत्तम। प्रासासिबाणकलिलं वर्तमाने सुदारुणे॥९२॥
verses.english: Thus took place that battle, ( best of Bharatas, in which no consideration was shown by any body for any one and in which lances, swords and arrows dropped down fast on every side and presented a terrific spectacle. Thus took place that battle, ( best of Bharatas, in which no consideration was shown by any body for any one and in which lances, swords and arrows dropped down fast on every side and presented a terrific spectacle.
